Por Chon uses a daily 19:00 cutoff. For each completed cutoff window, if the highest H4 wick/high made before 19:00 exceeds the previous Por Chon high frame by more than 1,000 project points, that highest H4 high becomes the new Por Chon New-High/ATH frame; otherwise keep the prior frame. Post-19:00 movement rolls into the next cutoff window.

Core cutoff/high-selection/>1000 semantics are therefore first-party Por Chon teaching, while the YouTube Show transcript still carries ASR risk. Asia/Bangkok mapping is a project contextual interpretation, not a literal timezone quote.

claims.canonical_statement: The source explicitly teaches two SIG-entry modes. Mode 1: after PA confirmation, enter during body collection while the prospective post-SIG candle is still forming; structural SL reference is the longest PA wick, or a nearby source-defined frame when applicable. Mode 2: after the post-SIG candle confirms and its wick becomes the point-check, enter on the following candle/body-collection move; for the discussed setup the confirmed post-SIG wick, point-check and structural SL reference are the same structural reference, with nearby source-defined frame routing when applicable. Example point buffers are contextual, not universal.

claims.canonical_statement: Current first-party/source video evidence supports multiple Sideway frame representations rather than one universal OHLC formula. A BODY_PRIMARY/body-only preference is explicitly taught in one source; another source uses a body core with optional wick structural layer/envelope because higher-timeframe wicks may encode lower-timeframe body structure. Sideway is dynamic, may expand and contain multiple support/resistance levels, and old resistance/support can role-flip after confirmed exit/retest. Full visible wick extrema and fixed width are not universal boundaries.

claims.canonical_statement: EP.5 teaches Body Collection as a forecast-zone method built from ซอก + ไส้ + คู่, not as one exact entry price. Use same-timeframe structure first; if unavailable, fall back one timeframe (e.g. H4->H1 and, when still incomplete, H1->M30). The current lesson uses two projected zones. Zone arrival alone is insufficient: lower-timeframe PA aligned with the H4 thesis and brake/confirmation context are required before entry consideration; no PA means no entry even inside the zone. Normal Body Collection is distinct from Sideway entry handling.
